title: Console-driven trace sampling override API and collector hook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a Console-driven sampling override mechanism that lets operators temporarily increase or decrease sampling rates for a tenant or route and have the collector honor a short-lived override token. This is intended to make it possible to triage spikes and investigate regressions without changing long-lived sampling policies or redeploying config. The feature includes: an API endpoint in the Control Plane that issues scoped override tokens, Console UI to request/apply overrides, and a lightweight collector hook that validates tokens and applies runtime sampling adjustments without restarting pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane API can issue scoped override tokens tied to tenant id, route pattern, ttl (max 15 minutes), and optional sample_rate override.
Collector accepts override token via OTLP header X-RW-Override and applies in-memory sampling override for matching spans for the token duration.
Console UI exposes a one-click workflow to request and apply an override with an auditable event stored in the tenant audit log.
Metrics emitted: override_requests_total, override_applied_total, override_denied_total, override_duration_seconds (histogram).
End-to-end integration tests validate token issuance, collector acceptance, and that spans during override reflect the requested sampling rate.
Security review completed and KMS-backed signing key rotation plan exists for override tokens.
implementation_notes: Token format: signed JWT with claims {tenant, route_pattern, issued_at, exp, sample_rate, nonce} signed by control-plane key. Collector validates signature and TTL.
Fallback behavior: if collector cannot validate token (clock skew, key missing), it should reject override and emit override_denied_total with reason tag.
Routing: override applies at collector processing stage before sampling decision; existing tenant-level sampling config should be preserved and override treated as temporary additive policy.
Rate limiting: control plane limits override issuance per-tenant to avoid abuse (default 3 concurrent overrides).
Operator UX: Console will show active overrides and allow early revoke via API.
Performance target: validation + in-memory lookup to add <0.5ms P95 overhead to span ingest path under typical load.
risks: Token leakage could be used to flood collector with high-sampling requests — mitigated by short TTLs (max 15m) and per-tenant rate limits.
Clock skew between control plane and collector can cause valid tokens to be rejected — mitigate via 2m leeway in validation and sync checks in deployment docs.
Collector complexity increase may introduce bugs in hot code paths — plan small canary, load tests, and circuit-breaker to auto-disable override hook if error rate > threshold.

qa_plan: Unit tests for token validation edge cases (expired, malformed, wrong tenant, wrong nonce).
Integration test: control plane issues token -> collector accepts header -> sampled fraction changes for test service (assert sample_rate within 5% of requested).
Load test: validate <0.5ms P95 overhead at 100k RPS with 50% requests carrying tokens.
Chaos: disable JWKS endpoint to confirm collector degrades gracefully and stops accepting new overrides while serving existing ones until they expire.
